Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects.

For the weighted RT functor of [[thm-weighted-rt-tqft-and-factorization]] and any complex modular ribbon fusion category, simple labels $i_1,\ldots,i_n$ and genus $g\ge0$, $$\dim V(\Sigma_g;i_1,\ldots,i_n)=\sum_{x\in I}S_{0x}^{\,2-2g-n}\prod_{r=1}^nS_{i_rx}.$$

The weight-zero positive Hopf mapping cylinder and positive core-twist cylinder have respectively the geometric classes $$s_+=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad t=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$$ (columns are the images of $m,l$), and their operators are $$S_{ji}=s_{ji}/D,\qquad T_{ji}=\delta_{ji}\theta_i.$$
For this positive Hopf/core-twist pair the exact relations are $$S^2=C,\qquad(ST)^3=\kappa I,\qquad C_{ji}=\delta_{j,i^*}.$$

For every compatible circle cut there is a natural factorization isomorphism $$V(\Sigma_{\rm glued};\vec W)\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}V(\Sigma_{\rm cut};\vec W,i,i^*).$$ The sewing map from right to left is the actual normalized tube map; its inverse is the complete composition-dual cutting resolution.
For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.
In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

derivations.claim: Apply [F2] with no marked labels to the state space defined in [L1] and [F1]. It gives $\dim_{\mathbb C}V(\Sigma_g)=\sum_{i\in I}S_{0i}^{2-2g}$ for every $g\ge0$, with the specified algebraic normalization and no conjugation. The torus part of [F3] has the matched hypotheses $\omega(m,l)=1$ and $\alpha=\lambda=\mathbb Rm$; [F4] gives the anomaly-bearing relation for these positive classes and the distinct inverse-generator relation after replacing the positive Hopf class by its inverse.

For $g=0$, [L1] gives $V(\Sigma_0)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)$, since $H^{\otimes0}=\mathbf1$. The unit is simple over $\mathbb C$ by [F1], so this Hom space is $\mathbb C$ and the sphere state space has dimension one. For each $i\in I$, the braiding unit axioms make the double braiding with label $0$, after the canonical unit identifications, the identity of $i$. The trace convention in [F1] therefore gives $s_{0i}=d_i$, and hence $S_{0i}=d_i/D$. By [F6] and [F7], both $d_i$ and $D$ are nonzero, so every $S_{0i}$ is nonzero. Thus the $g=1$ instance of [F2] has each term $S_{0i}^{0}=1$, and the torus dimension is $|I|$. Its basis $b_i$ is the one specified by [F2].

For any compatible cut, [F5] supplies the actual normalized tube map from the direct sum of the simple dual-label channels and its complete composition-dual cutting inverse, including separating and nonseparating cuts, all multiplicities, commuting disjoint cuts, and iterated gluing. Thus the maps in the statement are mutually inverse on the specified state spaces; the diagram only records that already-proved interface.

The weighted RT model is this category, these finite-dimensional complex state spaces, and the exact surgery-defined symmetric monoidal functor $Z$ of the supplied theorem.
A unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$.

derivations.claim: In the formula of [F2], increasing $n$ to $n+1$ leaves the Maslov correction, surgery signature, colored graph operator, boundary data, and cap normalization unchanged, and replaces the factor $\kappa^n$ by $\kappa^{n+1}$. Hence $Z(M,n+1)=\kappa Z(M,n)$.

Suppose the assignment factored as $Z=\overline Z\circ U$ through the forgetful operation $U$ on weighted bordisms. Since $U(M,n+1)=U(M,n)$, factorization would give $Z(M,n+1)=Z(M,n)$. With step 1.1 this yields $(\kappa-1)Z(M,n)=0$. A nonzero vector in the complex vector space of linear maps cannot be annihilated by a nonzero scalar, so $\kappa=1$, contradicting $\kappa\ne1$. Therefore no such factorization exists under the stated nonzero-map condition.

boundaries.evidence: The weighted RT theorem includes empty ends and the statement also applies when the fixed bordism data have empty boundary; the scalar comparison is step 1.1.
If Z(M,n)=0, the nonzero-map premise fails and no obstruction is claimed; the conditional is explicit in the Statement and step 2.1.
When kappa=1, the one-step weight comparison is weight-invariant and the proposition asserts no obstruction; see step 2.1.
The argument divides by no power of kappa and uses only (kappa-1)Z=0; the scalar case kappa=0 is covered by step 2.1 whenever the stated nonzero map exists.
The integer n is arbitrary and the supplier's weight-action law applies to every increment n to n+1; see step 1.1.
Full AC and inherited countable choice are stated in A1 and retained for the root weighted RT theorem in step 1.1; the scalar contradiction uses no stronger choice.

No converse claim that kappa=1 guarantees every unweighted construction is asserted.

Let $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, and let $\mathcal C_\ell$ be the standard ribbon semisimplification of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for Lusztig's divided-power $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, using the positive-trace quantum ribbon convention.

derivations.claim: Since $k\ge1$, $\ell=k+2\ge3$. By [F1], the actual quotient is modular and its label set is $I=\{0,\ldots,\ell-2\}=\{0,\ldots,k\}$, with the displayed $S$ matrix under the positive-trace convention. For each $a\in I$, $S_{0a}=\sqrt{2/\ell}\sin((a+1)\pi/\ell)\ne0$ because $0<(a+1)\pi/\ell<\pi$.
The genus-one formula in [F2] has exponent zero and therefore contributes one for each of the $k+1$ nonzero entries just identified. Thus $\dim V(T^2)=|I|=k+1$.

For $k=1$, $\ell=3$ and $S_{00}=S_{01}=\sqrt{2/3}\sin(\pi/3)=1/\sqrt2$. Applying [F2] gives, for every $g\ge0$,
$$\dim V(\Sigma_g)=2\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)^{2-2g}=2\cdot2^{g-1}=2^g.$$
The exponent formula is valid also at $g=0$, and no limiting or path-integral argument is used.

finite_checks.calculation: ell=3 and both S_0a entries are 1/sqrt(2).
finite_checks.result: The finite two-term sum is 2^g for every g>=0 by step 3.1.
